text:
Open-source SEO monitoring for founders, not SEO specialists

Google Search Console, a site crawler, Core Web Vitals and an MCP server in one self-hosted dashboard. Free and open source (MIT).

 
 
 
 

 

---

 
 
 

 Why crawlseo?

 crawlseo 
 --- --- 
 Price Free and open source (MIT) 
 Self-hosted ✅ Runs on your server, with Docker Compose or manually 
 Database On your machine (your own PostgreSQL) 
 GSC integration ✅ 
 Site crawler ✅ Up to 2,000 pages per crawl by default ( CRAWL MAX PAGES ) 
 Core Web Vitals ✅ 
 MCP server ✅ Read-only: no tool writes, changes, queues or triggers anything 
 Keyword research ✅ (BYOK) 
 Backlinks ✅ (BYOK) 

 BYOK = Bring Your Own Key. Keyword research and backlink data use DataForSEO (optional). Google Autocomplete suggestions work as a free fallback.

In Domain overview , enter a competitor's domain or full website URL and choose Compare to query DataForSEO for that domain. Search Console fallback data is only used for your own site; unavailable competitor metrics are shown as unavailable.

 Your data stays yours

crawlseo runs on your server. Your sites, keywords, crawl results and Google tokens stay in your database. We never receive them, and the app sends no usage statistics.

The app talks to outside services only in these cases:

 Destination When What is sent How to turn it off 
 --- --- --- --- 
 Google (sign-in, Search Console, PageSpeed Insights) When you sign in, connect Google, add a site or sync, run a vitals or index status check, inspect a URL through /api/v1 or the MCP, or disconnect Google. Also on the schedule: a GSC sync per site each day and a vitals check per site each week, or as often as you set in Settings Schedule Requests for your own properties and pages Don't run syncs, vitals or index status checks or URL inspections, or disconnect Google in Settings Connections. For the schedule: vitals checks Off in Settings Schedule, SCHEDULE GSC SYNC HOURS=0 , SCHEDULE VITALS DAYS=0 or SCHEDULER ENABLED=false 
 Bing Webmaster Tools Only if you add your own Bing API key; then also a sync per site each day Requests for your own Bing sites Remove the key in Settings Connections, or SCHEDULE BING SYNC HOURS=0 
 DataForSEO Only if you add your own DataForSEO key The keyword and domain queries you run Remove the key in Settings Connections 
 Google autocomplete Keyword suggestions when DataForSEO is not set up The seed keyword you typed Don't use keyword suggestions 
 Sites you crawl When you start a crawl, and on the schedule a crawl of each site each week, or as often as you set in Settings Schedule (Docker) Normal HTTP requests from your server, to the site and to the addresses its redirects point to Don't start a crawl; for the schedule: crawls Off in Settings Schedule, SCHEDULE CRAWL DAYS=0 or SCHEDULER ENABLED=false 
 Your alert webhook Only if you set a webhook URL in Settings Alert webhook: when alerts fire, and when you click Send test A signed JSON POST with the alerts that fired (type, message, site id and domain), to your own URL only Remove the webhook in Settings; ALERT WEBHOOKS ENABLED=false turns webhooks off for the whole instance 
 Your SMTP server Only if the operator sets SMTP HOST and SMTP FROM and you turn on Settings Email alerts: when alerts fire, and when you click Send test An email with the alerts that fired (type, message and domain, plain text and simple HTML, no tracking, links only to this instance), through the SMTP server the operator set, to the addresses you entered Turn off Email alerts in Settings; ALERT EMAILS ENABLED=false or no SMTP HOST turns email off for the whole instance 
 GitHub releases API Once a day A request for the latest crawlseo release. No data about you or your instance. GitHub sees your server's IP address CRAWLSEO UPDATE CHECK=false 

Nothing else leaves your server. Alerts are shown in the app, sent to your webhook if you set one, and emailed through the operator's own SMTP server if you turn that on. Nothing goes through a crawlseo service.

The hosts behind these rows are accounts.google.com , oauth2.googleapis.com , www.googleapis.com , searchconsole.googleapis.com , ssl.bing.com , api.dataforseo.com , suggestqueries.google.com and api.github.com , plus the sites you crawl, the webhook URL you set yourself and the SMTP server the operator sets in SMTP HOST . The list the tests check new code against is outbound-hosts.json . Your Google profile picture, if you have one, is loaded by your browser from Google, not by the server.

 Features

 🔍 GSC Analytics

Keywords, pages, clicks, impressions, position tracking with 28-day comparison and delta indicators.

 
 
 
 Top keywords with position badges, clicks, impressions, and CTR 
 

 🕷️ Site Crawler

Crawl up to 2,000 pages by default ( CRAWL MAX PAGES sets the server's limit) with concurrent fetching. Health score, 16 issue types, content scoring, and remediation guidance.

The crawler ( CrawlSEOBot/1.0 (+ follows robots.txt per RFC 9309: each host (the bare domain and www included) is checked against its own robots.txt, redirect targets are checked before they are followed, a robots.txt that answers 429 or 5xx, times out or fails with a network error skips that host, and Crawl-delay is honoured. The crawl page lists what robots.txt kept it from.

Pages marked noindex are crawled but not scored. A page counts as noindex when a or tag, or the X-Robots-Tag response header (for all crawlers or googlebot: ), says noindex or none ; directives for other crawlers are ignored, and when the tag and the header disagree, noindex wins. Its links are still followed ( noindex, follow is common), but it has no issues and does not count toward the health score, the issue counts or the content average, in the app, in /api/v1 and in the MCP tools. The crawl page shows how many there were and a noindex filter on the crawled pages, so an accidental noindex is easy to spot. A broken page is still reported as broken, noindex or not. install.title: Quick Start
install.html:
git clone https://github.com/crawlseo/crawlseo.git
cd crawlseo
cp .env.example .env.local
# Add your Google OAuth credentials to .env.local
docker compose up -d db
npm install
npx prisma migrate dev --name init
npm run dev

Open http://localhost:3000, sign in with Google, and add your first site.

🔑 Getting Google OAuth credentials
  1. Go to Google Cloud Console
  2. Create a project (or select existing)
  3. Enable the Google Search Console API
  4. Go to Credentials → Create Credentials → OAuth 2.0 Client ID
  5. Application type: Web application
  6. Authorized redirect URI: http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/google
  7. Copy Client ID and Client Secret to .env.local

Required scopes: openid, email, profile, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/webmasters.readonly

features.title: Features
features.html:
🔍 GSC Analytics

Keywords, pages, clicks, impressions, position tracking with 28-day comparison and delta indicators.


Top keywords with position badges, clicks, impressions, and CTR

🕷️ Site Crawler

Crawl up to 2,000 pages by default (CRAWL_MAX_PAGES sets the server's limit) with concurrent fetching. Health score, 16 issue types, content scoring, and remediation guidance.

The crawler (CrawlSEOBot/1.0 (+https://crawlseo.cloud/bot)) follows robots.txt per RFC 9309: each host (the bare domain and www included) is checked against its own robots.txt, redirect targets are checked before they are followed, a robots.txt that answers 429 or 5xx, times out or fails with a network error skips that host, and Crawl-delay is honoured. The crawl page lists what robots.txt kept it from.

Pages marked noindex are crawled but not scored. A page counts as noindex when a <meta name="robots"> or <meta name="googlebot"> tag, or the X-Robots-Tag response header (for all crawlers or googlebot:), says noindex or none; directives for other crawlers are ignored, and when the tag and the header disagree, noindex wins. Its links are still followed (noindex, follow is common), but it has no issues and does not count toward the health score, the issue counts or the content average, in the app, in /api/v1 and in the MCP tools. The crawl page shows how many there were and a noindex filter on the crawled pages, so an accidental noindex is easy to spot. A broken page is still reported as broken, noindex or not. Crawls from before this change keep the score they were given.


Crawl results with health score, issue breakdown, and per-page audit data

🤖 MCP server: AI agent integration

9 read-only tools for AI agents such as Claude Code, over HTTP at /mcp or over stdio, with access keys from Settings. Query your Search Console data, crawl issues, Core Web Vitals and opportunities without leaving the terminal. See MCP.


MCP setup page with connection config, setup guides, and available tools

More features
Feature Description
⚡ Core Web Vitals LCP, CLS, INP, TTFB via PageSpeed Insights with mobile/desktop comparison
🔑 Keyword Research DataForSEO-powered keyword ideas with volume, difficulty, CPC. Free Google Autocomplete fallback
🔗 Backlinks Backlink profile, referring domains, anchor text, dofollow/nofollow analysis
📊 Rank Tracking Historical position snapshots with saved keywords and notes
💡 SEO Opportunities Striking distance keywords, low CTR, content decay, cannibalization detection
🔔 Alerts Traffic drops, position drops, low crawl health, sites that are mostly noindex and degraded vitals. Checked after each sync and crawl and when you press Evaluate now, shown in the app, and sent to your webhook and email if you set them up
📥 CSV Export Export keywords and pages data for offline analysis

GSC sync, crawls and Core Web Vitals checks run when you start them in the app. There is no built-in schedule yet.
